classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied centre/radius joins to partition the triangle into three triangles with common perpendicular height, then factor their area sum.

content.prompt:
The circle in the diagram is called the incircle of triangle ABC. It touches the three sides of $\triangle ABC$ at P, Q and R. Prove that:
$$\text{Area of triangle}=\frac12\times(\text{perimeter of triangle})\times(\text{radius of circle}).$$
You will need to join the radii OP, OQ and OR and the intervals OA, OB and OC, where O is the centre of the incircle.

spec.description: Incircle tangent to BC at P, AC at Q and AB at R. Centre and auxiliary segments intentionally absent as in source; question asks students to add them.
spec.answerVisibility: Original supplied givens and targets only; no derived numerical values or proof conclusions.

answer.worked:
Join OP, OQ, OR, OA, OB and OC. Each radius to a point of tangency is perpendicular to the corresponding side. Let the common radius be r. The three triangles AOB, BOC and COA partition ABC, so
$$\begin{align*}A_{ABC}&=\frac12 AB\cdot OR+\frac12 BC\cdot OP+\frac12 CA\cdot OQ\\&=\frac12r(AB+BC+CA)\\&=\frac12\times\text{perimeter}\times\text{radius}.\end{align*}$$
